items.title: 3 Dividend Kings Retirees Can Own for the Rest of Their Lives
items.summary: Nearly two centuries of combined dividend raises sit behind three household names, yet each one carries a catch that could trim your future payouts. Which risk matters most, and which stock asks you to pay a record price for safety?

items.title: Investors 50 and Older Can Put $8,600 Into a Roth IRA in 2026 to Build Tax-Free Dividend Income
items.summary: Four household-name dividend stocks can quietly hand the IRS a four-figure bill every year, and one of them does most of the damage. Investors over 50 hold a special tool to fight back, but income limits can shut some couples out.

items.title: Big Yields Are Easy to Find. These 4 Dividend Stocks Cover Theirs With Cash to Spare
items.summary: A fat yield means little if the cash behind it runs thin. Four dividend payers, from a pipeline giant to a burger empire, pass a stricter test, though each carries one risk that could squeeze its next raise.

items.title: Can Oncology Emerge as Eli Lilly's Next Major Growth Driver?
items.summary: Lilly's oncology pipeline features eight potential medicines and new indications that could shape its next major growth opportunity.

items.title: What Could Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) FDA Cancer Approval Change For Investors?
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) received FDA accelerated approval for RYBREVANT FASPRO for advanced head and neck cancer in adults. The therapy is cleared for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after platinum chemotherapy and anti-PD-(L)1 treatment. RYBREVANT FASPRO is described as a first in class, dual targeted option for patients with limited second line treatment choices. items.title: Chevron Cut Its Debt by $8.4 Billion. These 4 Dividend Stocks Have Fortress Balance Sheets
items.summary: When the next recession hits, only some dividends survive the squeeze. Four companies from four different sectors passed a strict balance sheet test, but one of them carries a red flag that makes retirees look twice.
